issue_paraphrase: Stashing with the --include-untracked flag while passing a glob pathspec fails partway through: git prints the 'Saved working directory and index state' message and creates the stash, but then errors out with 'fatal: pathspec ... did not match any files' (the glob prefix is dropped from the pathspec), exits non-zero, and leaves the untracked files in the working tree. The stash command should succeed and remove the matched files from the worktree.
fix_summary: In the built-in stash, the pathspecs handed to the internal `git add`/`git diff-index`/`git ls-files` child processes were the parsed (match) form, which strips magic prefixes like ':(glob)'. The fix parses the stash pathspecs with PATHSPEC_PREFIX_ORIGIN and passes each pathspec's `original` form so the magic is preserved and the pathspec still matches.

issue_paraphrase: When creating a note with an explicit empty body — e.g. `git notes add -C <blob> --allow-empty`, `-m ""`, or `-F /dev/null` with `--allow-empty` — git unexpectedly launches the configured editor even though the note contents were supplied on the command line. In a non-interactive environment the editor invocation fails with 'error: there was a problem with the editor ...' and the note cannot be stored. Notes whose contents were fully provided on the command line should never open an editor, with or without --allow-empty.
fix_summary: Restored the pre-2023 behavior: the editor should only be invoked when the note message was not supplied via -m/-F/-c/-C options. The fix decides based on the message count (note_data.msg_nr) instead of the accumulated buffer length (which is 0 for empty contents) and removes the now-unneeded 'given' flag. Root cause was 90bc19b3ae (2023-05) which switched to a zero-length buffer check.
notes: The regression was introduced by 90bc19b3ae and affects any caller that supplies empty note contents non-interactively. t3301 is the big notes suite: a full run takes a few minutes at 64 cores (expect ~5-15 min at 1 CPU); all other tests in the file must pass. The resolver has a short, self-contained direct repro (git init + commit + notes add -C) that needs no network and no special prereqs.

issue_paraphrase: Running `git fetch --multiple --jobs=0` crashes git with an internal BUG diagnostic ('BUG: ... you must provide a non-zero number of processes!') and an abort signal rather than doing anything useful. The documented behavior for a parallel fetch setting of 0 is to fall back to a sensible default (the number of CPUs), which also used to be the behavior of `--jobs=0`; after a refactor it started aborting instead. The command should succeed using the default parallelism.
fix_summary: cmd_fetch() now treats --jobs=0 like fetch.parallel=0: `if (!max_jobs) max_jobs = online_cpus();` before running the parallel fetch machinery, so run_processes_parallel is never called with 0 processes. Root cause: 51243f9 (2022-10) removed the online_cpus fallback for explicit 0 values.
notes: Very clean, self-contained, no network needed (local remotes). t5514 is quick (<1 min at 64 cores; <2 min at 1 CPU). The BUG message names run-command.c plus the exact option, so the resolver will quickly locate `run_processes_parallel`/`pp_init`; the fix is the one-liner in builtin/fetch.c.

issue_paraphrase: Cloning a repository straight from a local path crashes when the source repository contains a ref file that is malformed (its contents are not a valid hexadecimal object id): the clone prints internal 'BUG: ... create called without valid new_oid' diagnostics and dies with a core dump instead of reporting a normal error. The clone should fail cleanly with an ordinary error message and a normal exit status, leaving no crash artifacts. The same crash happens for any local clone that reads such a ref during the clone.
fix_summary: ref_transaction_create() no longer calls BUG('create called without valid new_oid'); it appends "'<refname>' has a null OID" to the error strbuf and returns 1. Both callers already check the return value and die() with that message, so the user gets a graceful 'fatal: ...' error.
notes: Root cause is on the server side: local clone scans $GIT_DIR/refs and passes entries with null OIDs; GIT_REF_PARANOIA (default since 2.36) makes it always reproducible. t5605 is fast (<1 min at 64 cores). Note the failing ref in the golden test is 'refs/heads/topic' while the direct repro error names 'refs/remotes/origin/topic' (clone writes remote-tracking refs first) - the golden test only greps for the 'has a null OID' substring. No special prereqs.
